newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - BROKERS LEAD THE WAY.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - BROKERS LEAD THE WAY.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN
Insurance broking is dead - long live risk services. Such was the view expressed this week by one of the world's leading insurance brokers.
It is a view which is clearly shared by many of the top broking companies as they strive to become global consultants and yet retain superiority as specialists in their chosen areas.

Driven by the increasingly sophisticated and complex demands of their clients, Aon says brokers should be looking at how to repackage risk, commoditise insurance and bring in the financial markets, all with the aid of technology.
The brokers, at least those which will continue to be successful in the global market, are embracing these opportunities wholeheartedly in the knowledge that only the fittest will survive.
But, for every step the new broker consultants take towards finding innovative client solutions, the further they move into the world of alternative risk transfer and financing methods.
At present, it is the brokers who are making some of the most significant progress in these areas. They are taking them seriously because their clients are asking them to.

Some insurers and reinsurers are also making good progress. For the moment some are dabbling in some of the techniques and making necessary investment so they can hit the ground running when the need arises.
Others, on the other hand, seem happy to sit back and dismiss non-traditional risk solutions as 'niche' areas which will never take off.

They could be right. There will after all continue to be an increase in insurable risks and emerging markets will open up. But who is to say that these will automatically fall into the hands of the old-style insurers and reinsurers.
At least some of the innovative risk financing solutions are bound to become more widespread because it is in the interests of the world's most powerful brokers to ensure they do.
CEO of Aon Holdings Asia Bernard Fung said this week that brokers should only be one-and-a-half steps ahead of the clients because if they are three steps ahead the client is lost.
Surely then the insurers and reinsurers should only be one-and-a-half steps behind the brokers or they too could be lost.
